newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin cancels Dutch trip - Kremlin.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin cancels Dutch trip - Kremlin.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin has cancelled a visit to the Netherlands on the orders of his doctors, a Kremlin spokesman said on Monday.
A spokesman said doctors had advised Yeltsin, who is recovering from pneumonia at an official residence outside Moscow, to refrain from air travel and to work at home.

"Because of this, agreement has been reached with the government of the Netherlands and the chairman of the European Union to postpone the visit to the Netherlands. It will take place in Moscow in the near future."
Yeltsin had been due to hold talks in The Hague with Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok on February 4. Kok is the current president of the European Union.
"On the recommendation of his doctors, the president of Russia has in mind to work where he is for now," the spokesman said, reading from a prepared statement.
Aides have said the president is recovering well from the pneumonia, which struck just two weeks after he returned to the Kremlin following a major heart operation.
They say he is following affairs of state and working on papers, including an address to both houses of the Russian parliament due to be delivered next month.
But Yeltsin has not been seen on television since he chaired a Kremlin meeting about relations with NATO on January 6.
